title: Chat app
summary: WebSockets keep connections open; pub/sub routes messages between gateways.

lesson.problem: Messages must reach the other person instantly. With plain HTTP the server can only answer requests; it cannot push a new message to a client.
why: A WebSocket is a long-lived, two-way connection, so the server can push messages the moment they arrive. Gateways hold those connections, often hundreds of thousands each.

Alice and Bob are usually connected to different gateways. When Alice sends a message, the chat service stores it and publishes it to a pub/sub channel; every gateway with a subscriber for that conversation delivers it.
A presence store tracks who is online and on which gateway. Offline users get the message from storage when they reconnect, or as a push notification.
takeaways: Connections are stateful: route by who is connected where, not by round-robin.
Persist first, then deliver, so no message is lost if delivery fails.
Use heartbeats to detect dead connections and keep presence accurate.
